body:
## The outcome

A track runs the way an operator expects a multi-agent system to run: **one orchestrator session**
holds the plan and **one isolated subagent per node** does the work, siblings in the same wave running
at once, results flowing back to the orchestrator and onto the board. The track still costs one slot.

## Today

A track is one session doing N things **in a row**. The runner brief (`src/track.js:292-357`) is
explicit: *"You execute all N tasks in this one session, in dependency order … Claim a node when you
are about to start it, and end it before you claim the next."* There is no fan-out, no isolation
between nodes, and a 7-node track carries every node's context in one window.

The slot model already matches the goal — `src/dispatch.js:566` counts sessions, and a track's nodes
are `coveredBy` the root, so a track is one slot however many nodes it holds. What is missing is the
execution model underneath it.

The one hard blocker is the tool allowlist: `CLAUDE_TOOLS` (`src/board.js:12`) has no `Agent`, and
workers launch with `--permission-mode dontAsk`, which denies an unlisted tool rather than prompting.
A runner cannot spawn a subagent today even if the brief told it to.

## What already exists to build on

- **The parallel frontier is computed.** `trackWaves` (`src/track.js:75`) groups nodes into waves of
  mutually-unblocked siblings; the brief just walks them one at a time.
- **Isolation exists.** Claude Code's Agent tool takes `isolation: "worktree"`, so each node gets its
  own worktree — required, because parallel subagents in one worktree fight over files.
- **The hooks are session-wide.** PreToolUse applies to subagent tool calls, so the permission policy
  holds inside children. The root's heartbeat already covers every node (`coveredBy`).
- **Disjoint `paths` are already enforced** by `/kanban:decompose` — the rule that keeps node dispatch
  safe keeps a wave safe.
- **Branch chaining carries over**: `git switch -c kb/<n> <base>` where `<base>` is the blocker's
  branch, exactly as the brief says today.

## Constraints

- `Agent` goes on the **`claude-track` profile only**. Cold node workers stay single-agent.
- Every node still ends with its own PR and its own terminal verb — that is what makes it a durable
  checkpoint, and it is what lets the ordinary dispatcher finish a track whose orchestrator died.
- The orchestrator must **verify each subagent recorded a verb** before moving to the next wave: the
  Stop-hook nudge keys on `KB_TASK`, which is the root, so it fires for the orchestrator, not for each
  child. That is a brief-level rule.
- Per-node identity must reach each subagent. Today `KB_TASK` does not reliably reach even the parent
  session (#125); whatever fix #125 takes — env, a worktree-name fallback, or the dispatcher resolving
  sessions at reap time — this goal depends on it and should be linked under it once #125 is promoted.
- `--max-budget-usd 5` and `--max-turns 80` on the launch (`src/board.js:30`) are sized for one node;
  a fanned-out track needs a bigger envelope, and the profile description already tells adopters to
  give a track a generous `max_runtime` — budget is the same sentence.
- The protocol stays backend-neutral: claim → work → verb, per node. Nothing here adds an LLM to the
  dispatcher; orchestration lives in the runner, which is already an LLM session.

## The pieces

- **A** — `Agent` on the `claude-track` allowlist, with the subagent hook behaviour verified against a
  real spawn: PreToolUse fires inside the child, `SubagentStop` vs `Stop` semantics understood, and a
  test that the `claude` profile still cannot spawn.
- **B** — the runner brief rewritten around `trackWaves`: claim the wave, spawn one isolated subagent
  per node with the node's `hkb context` as its brief, collect, verify verbs, next wave. Skip-on-block
  semantics preserved: a blocked node parks its dependents, the rest of the graph continues.
- **C** — `skills/kanban/references/protocol.md`, the `claude-track` profile description, and the
  README's track section describe the new model, including when to prefer a track over node dispatch
  now that a track also parallelises.

## Out of scope

Changing node dispatch. Cold workers stay one session, one node.

## Acceptance

A decomposed goal with a diamond (two path-disjoint siblings feeding one dependent) adopted as
`claude-track` runs both siblings **concurrently** inside one session, each in its own worktree, each
ending with its own PR and verb; the dependent starts only after both; the board shows one running
slot throughout; killing the orchestrator mid-track leaves claims the ordinary dispatcher reclaims and
finishes. `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Spike A — measured 2026-08-28 on Claude Code 2.1.251

Setup: `claude --bg --name "kb spike 129" --worktree kb-spike-129 --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources user --settings '<PreToolUse/SubagentStop/Stop logging hooks>' --allowedTools Agent 'Bash(*)' Write Read --model sonnet --max-turns 12 --max-budget-usd 2`. The root ran one Bash probe, called the Agent tool once with `isolation: "worktree"` and the same probe, and wrote the result. Job `cadca6f1`, subagent `aff2ce6259a1c9878`; every hook firing was logged with its payload and env.

| # | question | answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Can a `--bg --worktree` root spawn an isolated subagent under `dontAsk` with `Agent` allowed? | **Yes.** `AGENT_TOOL: ok`. The allowlist line is the whole unlock. |
| 2 | Where does the child's worktree live? | `.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>` **at the repo level** — a sibling of `kb-<n>-<k>`, not nested — on branch `worktree-agent-<id>`, common dir the repo's `.git`. It was **auto-removed with its branch** when the subagent ended unchanged, so a node subagent must commit and push before it returns. The name is Claude's, never `kb-<node>-<k>`: `parseWorktreeName` cannot identify the node from the checkout — the brief passes `<n>` explicitly, as it already does. |
| 3 | Which session does `hkb finish <node>` stamp from a child? | **The root's.** Inside the child, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` equal the root's (`cadca6f1…`, `~/.claude/jobs/cadca6f1`). #131's counted-once rule holds as designed. |
| 4 | Do `--settings` hooks fire inside the child? | **Yes.** `PreToolUse` fired for every child Bash call with `agent_id` set and `cwd` = the child worktree; `SubagentStop` fired with `agent_id`; `Stop` fired for the root only. The permission policy holds inside children. |
| 5 | Do subagent tokens reach the budget and the bill? | The child's usage is written to a **sidecar** — `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` — not into the parent transcript (root: 23 turns / 13,064 out; child: 18 turns / 254 out / 80k cache-write, in its own file). `src/stats.js` `usageFromTranscript` reads only `transcript_path`, so **subagent tokens are invisible to `hkb stats` today** (the "sidechain lines are counted" comment describes the older in-file format) → tracked on #155. Whether `--max-budget-usd` counts them could not be measured without exceeding it — unknown. The job record's `tokens` (6,435) is neither total. |

Two things the probe showed that were not on the list, both decisive for piece B:

- **The worktree-isolation guard refuses compound and `$VAR` commands — in the root and in the child.** `a; b` and even `echo "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"` were refused as *"too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"*; `printenv VAR` and single plain commands ran. This is the same guard behind the `complete`/heredoc refusals in `docs/harnesses.md`. The runner brief and the per-node subagent prompt must say: one command per Bash call, no `;`/`&&`, no `$VAR`, `printenv` for env.
- **The root ends its turn while a subagent runs, and `Stop` fires at that moment.** The Agent call ran in the background and the root parked itself with ScheduleWakeup; `Stop` fired before `SubagentStop`. hkb's Stop hook (`src/hook.js` `stopHook`) would see the root still `running` and answer `{decision: "block"}` with the terminal-verb nudge, twice per attempt, before any child is done. Piece B needs one of: the root waits on the wave synchronously (the Agent tool's foreground mode), or the hook recognises a track root with live subagents and does not nudge.

Also confirmed in passing: the host's session daemon still carried `KB_TASK=146` from an earlier launch (#150), and **both root and child inherited it** — the leak reaches subagents. The probe used `--setting-sources user` so the repo's hkb hooks stayed out of the measurement.
goal: a claude-track root runs its ready siblings concurrently as isolated subagents inside one slot
title: A track is an orchestrator with one isolated subagent per node, not one session doing N things in a row
